chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Descend from Al-Safa walking to Al-Marwa, and upon you should be tranquility and dignity until you reach the marker, which is at the edge of the Sa'ee area. So walk briskly (filling your chest with breath) and say: 'In the Name of Allah, and Allah is the Greatest, and may Allah send Blessings upon Muhammad and upon His Household. O Allah, forgive, have mercy, and overlook what You know, and You are the Mighty, the Benevolent' until you reach the other marker.

So when you pass it, say: 'O Possessor of Favor and Grace and Generosity and Blessings and Bounty, forgive my sins, for there is no Forgiver of sins except You.' Then walk, and upon you should be tranquility and dignity until you reach Al-Marwa. So climb upon it until the House (Kabah) appears to you, and do upon it as you did upon Al-Safa, and circumambulate between them seven circuits, beginning with Al-Safa and ending with Al-Marwa.

key_terms.الصَّفَا: Al-Safa, one of the two hills between which Sa'ee is performed
key_terms.الْمَرْوَة: Al-Marwa, the second of the two hills
key_terms.الْمَسْعَى: The place of Sa'ee, the area between the two hills
key_terms.الْمَنَارَة: The marker or landmark indicating the end of the brisk running section

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications and manner of walking during the Sa'ee between Safa and Marwa?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi provides the detailed fiqh and spiritual etiquette for Sa'ee, emphasizing the transition from dignified walking (Sakinah) to vigorous running (Mil'a Furuj) between the two markers, a practice rooted in the tradition of Prophet Ibrahim and his son Ismail. It prescribes specific supplications for forgiveness and divine grace at each end, reinforcing the ritual as an act of humble submission and remembrance of God's mercy. The instruction to face the Kaaba while standing on Al-Marwa connects the physical movement to the spiritual orientation of the believer.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Go down walking from Al-Safa to Al-Marwa, and upon you should be tranquility and the dignity until you come to the marker, and it is upon the side of the Sa’ee area. So walk briskly filled with relief and say, ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is the Greatest, and may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> send Blessings upon Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> and upon the People<sup>asws</sup> of his<sup>saww</sup> Household. O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Forgive, and be Merciful, and Overlook from what You<sup>azwj</sup> well Know, and You<sup>azwj</sup> are the Mighty, the Benevolent’ – until you reach the other marker.

So when you exceed it, say, ‘O One with the Favours, and the Grace, and the benevolence, and the Bounties, and the Generousity! Forgive my sins for me, for there is no Forgiver of sins except for You<sup>azwj</sup>’. Then walk, and upon you should be the tranquility and the dignity, until you come to Al-Marwa. So climb upon it until the House (Kabah) appears to you, and do upon it just as you had done upon Al-Safa, and circumambulate seven circuits between the two, beginning with Al-Safa and ending with Al-Marwa’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

climb down from al-Safa’, walking to al-Marwah in a calm and dignified manner up to the sign; then walk faster and say, ‘I begin by the help of the name of Allah, Allah is great beyond description. O Allah, I appeal before You to grant salawat (favors and compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause). O Allah, forgive me, be kind and merciful to me and ignore what You know (about me) and You are majestic and honorable.’ Then walk until you reach the other sign.

When you pass this sign say, ‘O munificent, generous, honorable, bountiful and benevolent, forgive my sins; no one is able to forgive sins except You.’ Then walk in a calm and dignified manner until you reach al-Marwah. Climb up until you can see the House, then do what you had done at al-Safa’, then walk between them seven times beginning from al-Safa’ to end at al-Marwah.’”
